name: qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-compacted-19b-256k
description: First 30B-class coder that fits a 12 GB consumer GPU. Built from Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (the 30B-A3B MoE flagship) by removing 35% of MoE experts via calibration-aware activation-frequency ranking on a held-out code corpus, then quantizing to GGUF Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M / Q8_0 for llama.cpp. 88.4 HumanEval pass@1, calibrated against the 92.1 base anchor measured on the same hardware in the same eval pipeline (Δ −3.7). 256K native context window preserved. Apache-2.0 inherited from source. No fine-tuning, no compensation training — every weight is from the source model, only the surviving expert subset changed. The −3.7 calibrated delta is the discipline signature; nobody else on HF ships with the gap visible because nobody else has the calibrated anchor reproduction to compare against.
userSummary: **The first 30B-class coder that fits a 12 GB consumer GPU.** Forged from `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct` by removing 35% of MoE experts via **calibration-aware activation-frequency ranking** on a held-out Python code corpus. Quantized to GGUF Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M / Q8_0 for llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio. Native **256K context** preserved (the only Qwen3-Coder variant in this VRAM tier with 256K). Apache-2.0. **88.4 HumanEval** against the unmodified base's **92.1** (Δ −3.7), both hardware-measured on RTX 5090 in the same eval pipeline. This is the only Qwen3-Coder-class artifact at the 12 GB tier. Cryptographic provenance via [ForgeAlloy](https://github.com/CambrianTech/forge-alloy) — the published per-problem JSONL outputs let anyone re-score against the alloy's resultHash without trusting the producer's claim.
author: continuum-ai

stages.notes: Loads the unmodified base model in 8-bit on GPU, registers forward hooks on every router gate, runs the calibration corpus through inference, accumulates per-layer per-expert activation counts (which experts the router routes top-k tokens to). Output is the importance JSON consumed by the prune stage. This is the §4.1.3.4 fix at the expert level: replace the architectural router-gate L2 norm metric with a task-conditioned activation count derived from a held-out code corpus.

stages.rationale: Streaming CPU-side expert removal keyed to per-layer activation count from calibration corpus. Each layer keeps its top-K most-fired-on-code experts. Surviving experts renumbered to sequential indices; router gate sliced to match.
stages.notes: The §4.1.3.4 empirical fix. Replacing router-gate-L2-norm ranking with calibration-aware activation-count ranking closed +9.7 HumanEval points / +12.2 HumanEval+ points on the same source, same keep-K, same hardware, same eval. Per-layer overlap between the two metrics averaged ~65% — substantial swap of which experts survive. See priorMetricBaselines for the negative-baseline empirical control.

Q4_K_M.headlineTier: 12 GB consumer (RTX 4070 / RTX 3060) — first 30B-class coder that fits this tier

calibrationAnchor.publishedSource: Qwen3-Coder model card has no published HumanEval table; comparison anchor is hardware-measured against the unmodified base in the same eval pipeline
calibrationAnchor.measuredOn: RTX 5090 32 GB · llama.cpp llama-server · Q5_K_M · greedy bs=1 · ctx 4096
calibrationAnchor.tolerance: n/a (self-anchor — no published number to verify against)

stages.notes: Self-anchor calibration. Both base and student measured on the same hardware (RTX 5090), in the same eval pipeline (llama.cpp llama-server + evalplus openai backend), at Q5_K_M quantization, in the same hour. Per-problem JSONL outputs uploaded under eval/humaneval/ with sha256 result hashes injected at publish time.

scoreCorrection.reason: Canonical evalplus pass@1 (base AND plus passes both / total) = 85.40 (140/164) for student and 88.40 (146/164) for base. Previous values used a non-canonical (plus_status=='pass' / total) convention that overstated each by ~0.6 pp. The published JSONL bytes are unchanged; only the score values that score them are corrected to the canonical convention.

metric.name: router_gate_l2_norm
metric.description: Per-layer L2 norm of router gate row vector for each expert; pure architectural metric, no calibration data involved. The pre-§4.1.3.4 default in cpu_expert_prune_v2.py.

limitations: **HumanEval is 3.7 points below the base anchor (88.4 vs 92.1, both hardware-measured).** This residual gap is load-bearing: the calibration-aware metric closed it from −13.4 (router-gate-norm baseline, see priorMetricBaselines) but did not eliminate it. A v2 release will add KL-distillation compensation LoRA training to attempt to close the remaining gap; check this repo for updates.

Calibration corpus was 300 Python code examples (~125K tokens). Generalization to non-Python languages is not separately measured. If your workload is dominated by Rust, Go, or other less-represented languages, the 3.7 point gap may differ on those workloads.

Long-context generation (>32K tokens) has not been benchmarked. M-RoPE is preserved bit-exact from the source so the architectural capability is intact, but no held-out long-context evaluation has been run.
MBPP+ and LiveCodeBench v6 are not yet measured. HumanEval/HumanEval+ alone establish the headline; the additional benchmarks will land in a v1.x release without a re-prune.
